next_step: Run 72-hour throughput soak on dedicated pool; finalize SLA draft with legal
notes: Overview: enterprise logistics SaaS using generative models for route summarization, dynamic reranking of carrier choices, and agent-facing chat assistants.
Primary ask: Dedicated capacity with predictable throughput plus per-route priority lanes to protect latency-critical agent flows during sales peaks.

Throughput/latency targets: p95 text-gen < 120ms, p99 < 350ms for agent chat (16-32 token responses); embeddings batch throughput target 4k vectors/min with 2s p95; reranking pipeline requires sustained 200 r/s at 128-token context.

Reserved GPU planning: initial request = 8x A100 equivalent (or compatible pool) for 2x redundancy; growth plan to 16 GPUs within 6 months tied to 3x monthly traffic growth. Want explicit reserved slot guarantees and predictable placement (no preemption).
SLA negotiations: legal requested formal latency SLOs for p95/p99 and credits for missed SLOs; also wants documented escalation path and performance report cadence (weekly for POC).

Traffic shaping & priority lanes: customer wants per-tenant priority lanes (agent->high, background indexing->low) with strict quotas per route, token & request-based rate limiting, and dynamic throttles when pool approaches saturation.

Noisy-neighbor controls: require opaque tenant isolation, ability to pin models to dedicated sub-pools, per-route CPU/GPU reservations, and automatic eviction/fallback policies for low-priority workloads. Ask: placement hints and fractional GPU QoS (soft reservation + preemptible burst) — Redwood asked about feasibility and kernel-level QoS options.

Security & compliance: full SSO/SAML integration, KMS-managed keys for model artifacts, audit logs retention 1 year, and data residency in NA. Security team requested answers to sec questionnaire (see drive doc).

POC plan: 3 phases — (1) smoke + connectivity + SSO (2) 72-hour throughput soak with synthetic traffic and two priority classes (3) user-traffic pilot with gradual cutover. Success criteria: sustained throughput within 10% of forecast, no p99 breaches >2/day, correct routing to priority lanes.

Recent activities: 2026-01-21 kickoff call (Priya/Luis) — infra diagram reviewed; 2026-02-10 deep-dive on traffic shaping (Fireflies ff_2026-02-10_irnwd_initial); 2026-02-18 bench readout + kernel questions (ff_2026-02-18_traffic-shaping).
Quote from CTO: 'We need guarantees — if agent flows slow, business ops stop. Can’t accept noisy bursts from batch jobs during peak hours.'

Technical concerns surfaced: opaque autoscaling behavior, head-of-queue latency when batching is aggressive, cache warm-up cold starts for large context models. SE to propose KV cache pre-warming strategy and per-route cache partitions.

Commercial notes: they prefer a committed monthly reserved fee with explicit burst credits; procurement flagged the need for PoP-level pricing to compare against internal infra costs. Finance wants 12-month contract with step-up capacity clause.

Open questions: 1) Can Redwood expose per-route telemetry for billing/alerts? 2) How are model fallbacks priced if primary model capacity exhausted? 3) Is fractional GPU QoS supported or only whole-node isolation?

Action items: SE (Luis) to define resource reservation policy doc by 2026-03-05; Infra eng to propose noisy-neighbor mitigation design; AE to circulate SLA redline v0.2 to Ironwood legal by 2026-03-03.
